title: The browser's Back leaves the landing instead of stepping back a level
body:
## Summary
The cosmos keeps a level stack (root > type|family > template|category) entirely in cx.ST, so the browser Back button or a phone's back gesture leaves the landing instead of stepping back one level.

## Description
app/_landing/cosmos/engine/nav.ts:129 navTo and nav.ts:189 back() move between levels without history.pushState/popstate; the only Back is the HUD button (Cosmos.tsx #back) and Esc (keyboard.ts). The app-shell golden path (software-engineering/ui-surfaces/shell-and-navigation/app-shell, technique navigation-model) requires history and back behavior to follow the shell's location; .ai/registry-map.json records this as a deviation at nav.ts:196, re-verified on this tree. Fixed: each level entry pushes a same-URL state carrying {lv,type,tpl,fam,cat}; popstate calls back() (or navTo the state); destroy() leaves the stack consistent. Hazard: Next's app router owns popstate on this page, so the state must be marked and ignored by it (or handled before it).

## Flow
- open a type, then a template on a phone
- press the system back gesture
- observed: the tab leaves / to the previous site; expected: the template closes to its type
- build: a history adapter in nav.ts (push on setLv deeper, replace on sideways), popstate -> back(cx), a guard so Next's router does not re-render the route

## Expected impact
Every phone visitor who uses the back gesture inside the cosmos stops losing the page; measured as Back presses needed to return from a template to the overview (today: the page is gone after 1). Could break: Next app-router navigation on popstate, double steps if both the HUD Back and history move.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the platform Back steps one level, as the HUD Back does
Before: Back presses from root>type>template to root that stay on the landing: 0 (the first leaves the site)
After: predicted 2 of 2 (template -> type -> root), a third leaves
Method: simulation - walked on nav.ts; the rung above needs a history fake plus Next's popstate behaviour, an M instrument, not built this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: app/_landing/cosmos/engine/nav.ts:129-187 (navTo: no history), app/_landing/cosmos/engine/nav.ts:189-199 (back), .ai/registry-map.json landing-cosmos-shell app-shell state=deviation
instrument: tests/next-server/landing-cosmos-engine.test.ts: a fake history (pushState/replaceState/popstate) around navTo/back; count Back presses from template to overview that stay on the page (0 today, 2 after); plus a check that Next's router state is left untouched

title: The search slip is a dialog and a listbox in name only
body:
## Summary
The search slip says role=dialog but keeps no focus inside it, and its results are buttons whose keyboard highlight (.sel) is never exposed to assistive technology.

## Description
app/_landing/cosmos/Cosmos.tsx:102-110 renders #search role=dialog with an input and a ul; app/_landing/cosmos/engine/search.ts:40-58 renderRes marks the chosen result with class 'sel' only, and keyboard.ts moves cx.sel on the arrows while the focus stays in the input. A screen reader hears the typed query and nothing of the results or which one Enter will pick; Tab from the input walks out of the slip into the HUD and scene behind the scrim. Fixed: the input is role=combobox with aria-expanded / aria-controls=res / aria-activedescendant, the results are role=option with ids and aria-selected; Tab and Shift+Tab stay within #search (or Tab closes it).

## Flow
- press '/', type 'mu'
- ArrowDown twice: the third result is highlighted visually
- a screen reader announces nothing; Tab lands on the HUD behind the scrim

## Expected impact
Screen-reader and keyboard users can search the landing; measured as the accessibility tree's active option (none today) and Tab stops outside #search while open. Could break: the pointer-move highlight sync and the Enter pick.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the active result is announced and the focus stays in the slip
Before: attributes exposing the active result: 0 of 3 (role, aria-activedescendant, aria-selected); Tab targets outside #search while open: all of them
After: predicted 3 of 3; 0 outside
Method: simulation - read on the markup; the fake DOM in landing-cosmos-engine.test.ts can take both figures, not built in this round's budget
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: app/_landing/cosmos/Cosmos.tsx:102-110; app/_landing/cosmos/engine/search.ts:40-58 (class 'sel' only); app/_landing/cosmos/engine/keyboard.ts:20-38 (sel moves, focus stays in #q)
instrument: the DomEl fake in tests/next-server/landing-cosmos-engine.test.ts: openSearch, type, ArrowDown; assert #q aria-activedescendant names a role=option with aria-selected=true; dispatch Tab from the last result and assert the focus stays inside #search

title: Opening a template or a category leaves the focus on a now-inert card
body:
## Summary
openTpl and openCat keep the focus on the card or tile that opened them, which setLv then makes inert, so the browser drops the focus to <body> and the stage that opened is not reached by the next Tab.

## Description
app/_landing/cosmos/engine/nav.ts:37-56 setLv sets els.typeView.inert for lv tpl and els.libView.inert for lv cat; app/_landing/cosmos/engine/carousel.ts:313-326 openTpl and app/_landing/cosmos/engine/library.ts:174-189 openCat focus nothing on the stage. The app-shell golden path: navigation moves focus into the new content. Fixed: after the stage renders, focus its title strip (tabindex=-1) or its first control. carousel.ts and library.ts belong to landing-cosmos-paper-raster/scenes.

## Flow
- Tab to a template card, press Enter
- the stage opens; the card is inert; the focus falls to <body>
- Tab starts from the HUD

## Expected impact
Keyboard users land on what they opened; measured as document.activeElement inside #stageView after openTpl/openCat (no today). Could break: the flip animation reads the card rect before the focus moves.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - opening an item puts the focus on its stage
Before: focus inside #stageView after opening: 0 of 2 paths (template, category)
After: predicted 2 of 2
Method: simulation - walked on setLv/openTpl/openCat; the fake DOM would measure it, and the fix spans carousel.ts and library.ts (other contexts)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: app/_landing/cosmos/engine/nav.ts:52-54 (inert per level); app/_landing/cosmos/engine/carousel.ts:313-326 (openTpl: no focus); app/_landing/cosmos/engine/library.ts:174-189 (openCat: no focus)
instrument: DomEl fake: openTpl(cx, 0) / openCat(cx, 0) on a built type view / family sheet; assert els.stageView.contains(document.activeElement)

title: The reason chip and a sign-in error hang on the same spot below the pill
body:
## Summary
EnterButton's StaleBadge ('session ended') and its error line are both absolutely placed at right:0, top:calc(100% + 10px), so when both show they draw over each other.

## Description
app/_landing/cosmos/cosmos.css:185 '.pc .pc-enter-wrap>:not(.pc-enter){position:absolute;right:0;top:calc(100% + 10px)}' applies to both app/_landing/parts.tsx:101-103 (ended chip) and parts.tsx:104-108 (role=alert error). Both are visible when a redirect sign-in fails on return (lib/useAuth.tsx:138-140 sets error without a click) while lastTransition is session-ended or account-switched. Fixed: one absolutely placed column holding both (gap 8px), or the error below the chip.

## Flow
- session ends; the landing shows 'session ended'
- a redirect sign-in comes back failed: getRedirectResult rejects and sets error
- the error paragraph covers the chip

## Expected impact
A returning user sees both the reason and the error; measured as the overlap of the two boxes in px. Could break: the pill's level alignment with the search button (the column must stay out of flow).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the reason and the error are both legible
Before: overlap: the two boxes share their top-right corner (predicted ~chip height)
After: 0 px
Method: simulation - the HUD probe (static skeleton + cosmos.css + real fonts, headless Chromium) used for 50310dfe takes this figure with both children present; not run this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: the HUD probe from 50310dfe (scratch: static skeleton + app/_landing/cosmos/cosmos.css + .next-landing woff2 in headless Chromium) with .pc-enter-wrap holding the chip and the error; measure their box overlap

title: At 320 px the top-right row still overlaps the wordmark
body:
## Summary
After 50310dfe the overlap of #tr with the wordmark is 0 from 360 px up, but at 320 px it is 38 px signed out and 28 px signed in.

## Description
#wm ends at ~167 px (app/_landing/cosmos/cosmos.css #wm, font max(24px, S*.031)); #tr is the 46 px search button plus a pill of max(46px, S*.054) height with 18/20 px padding (cosmos.css:361). At 320 x 568 (iPhone SE 1st gen, small Androids) the two meet. Fixed: in portrait under ~340 px, a smaller wordmark or a pill that is the G mark alone (aria-label carries the name), or the HUD's navrow moved below the pill's height.

## Flow
- open / at 320 x 568, signed out
- the pill's left edge sits at 129 px, under the wordmark's last letters

## Expected impact
Visitors on the smallest phones read the wordmark; measured by the same HUD probe. Could break: the wordmark's size on other portrait widths if the rule is not bounded.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - nothing overlaps the wordmark at 320 px
Before: 38 px (signed out), 28 px (signed in) - probe
After: predicted 0 / 0
Method: probe for Before (the HUD probe, real fonts); After not built - the remedy is a design choice between three shapes
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: HUD probe after 50310dfe: 320x568 signed out wm 16-167 tr 129-304 overlap 38; signed in tr 139-304 overlap 28
instrument: the HUD probe from 50310dfe at 320 x 568, both auth states

title: The landing is the last consumer of v1's StaleBadge
body:
## Summary
app/_landing/parts.tsx imports StaleBadge from v1 components/ui/signal/StaleBadge.tsx, whose own header says the landing is its only caller; every other screen spells an amber chip through @gt/ui.

## Description
grep 'signal/StaleBadge' finds app/_landing/parts.tsx:12 and a comment in packages/ui/src/components/stalebadge/StaleBadge.tsx; components/ui/signal/StaleBadge.tsx:34-35 keeps v1 Tally's chip classes alive for that one caller. @gt/ui's StaleBadge is a freshness edge (stale/offline) and is the wrong meaning for 'session ended'; @gt/ui's Chip (tone amber, label, glyph) is the right shape. Fixed: parts.tsx renders the reason with @gt/ui Chip; the v1 file is deleted (components/ - out of this context's paths).

## Flow
- parts.tsx -> components/ui/signal/StaleBadge (v1 Tailwind chip)
- replace with @gt/ui Chip tone=amber; delete the v1 file

## Expected impact
One spelling of the amber chip instead of two; measured as v1 signal/ consumers (1 -> 0) and a kit/legibility check of the landing's chip. Could break: the chip's look on the paper landing (Tailwind vs @gt/ui tokens).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one chip vocabulary; a v1 file with one consumer retires
Before: consumers of components/ui/signal/StaleBadge: 1
After: 0, and the file deleted
Method: probe for Before (grep); After needs the deletion outside this context and a look at the landing
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: grep -rl 'signal/StaleBadge' app components lib = 0; the session-ended-reason probe still green; the HUD probe for the chip's box

title: The engine chunk's import has no catch in Cosmos.tsx
body: Rejected not-better. Cosmos.tsx:51 `void Promise.all([import("./engine"), ...]).then(...)` has no .catch. Before: a failed chunk or a throwing mountCosmos is reported once on the console (the browser's unhandled-rejection line with its stack), and the page stays at its first paint - the dusk sky, the wordmark and a working sign-in pill (parts.tsx needs no engine). After a .catch with a log: the same one console line, the same page. The figure (failures surfaced, user-visible state) is equal on both sides. The lazy-section-loading technique's chunk-failure honesty would ask for more than a log - a retry or a stated failure - which is a design call, not this finding.

title: rebuild() lets a scene build's throw escape where boot() catches it
body: Rejected not-better. intro.ts boot() wraps buildScene in try/catch; rebuild() (the resize and governor paths) does not. Before: a throw in the swap is an unhandled rejection the browser logs with its stack, the resize leaves the old picture CSS-scaled to cover, the governor stays off. After a catch + log + return false: one console line, the same scaled picture, the same governor. Equal figures on every dimension measured.
evidence: app/_landing/cosmos/engine/intro.ts:53-57 (boot catches) vs intro.ts:159 (rebuild awaits bare)
